messages:
ruth-oncall: eu-west-1 dedicated pool just hit 100% and we're spilling to hosted fallback. Seeing higher latencies and a few 502s for customers pinned to dedicated. I'm on it.

sre-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool-eu-west1 utilization=100% GPUs_in_use=48 total_gpus=48 fallback_route=active severity=high

devin-eng: thanks — can you paste the autoscaler logs? did autoscaler try to add nodes?

ruth-oncall: logs below (tail):
```
autoscaler[event] time=2026-03-18T10:05:12Z desired=50 current=48 pending=0 reason="image-pull-timeout, provisioning-queue"
autoscaler[event] time=2026-03-18T10:07:03Z desired=50 current=48 pending=2 reason="pending-spot-allocation"
```

leo-infra: looks like provisioning lag + spot allocation failures. We have pending=2 but they haven't come up. Are we getting any network timeouts to the cloud provider?

ruth-oncall: provider API errors in the last 12m: rate-limited + transient 500s. Provisioning estimate now ~12-18m.

anya-product: any customers impacted? @sam-sales can you check if any enterprise customers on dedicated in eu-west are seeing errors?

sam-sales: saw a support ticket from BigRetail EU complaining about 502s on batch inference. They have a Dedicated commitment, so high priority. I've DM'ed legal + acct.

devin-eng: interim mitigation: increase hosted fallback weight so traffic drains off dedicated while we spin nodes. We can adjust routing via control plane. Example: 
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","dedicated_weight":0.6}'
```
That sets dedicated to 60% and hosted to 40%.

leo-infra: can we instead do smarter routing: keep dedicated for pinned accounts (BigRetail) and fall back others to hosted? Need to preserve SLA for committed customers.

ruth-oncall: good call. I'm applying a rollback rule to keep routes for accounts with tag="dedicated-sla" pinned to dedicated. Others will go to hosted.

infra-deploy-bot: action=route-update region=eu-west-1 dedicated_weight=0.6 pinned_tags=["dedicated-sla"] status=applied ts=2026-03-18T10:09:40Z

devin-eng: also reducing batch sizes and throttling low-priority realtime jobs will free up tokens. Can we flip a soft-limit on large-batch endpoints?

ruth-oncall: enabled soft-limit on /v1/generate: max_batch_tokens=1024 -> 512 for non-SLA accounts.

leo-infra: cost note: hosted fallback is billed at on-demand rates. If we keep 40% for >1h, estimate +$3.2k/hr. We should try to keep fallback brief.

anya-product: we need comms to BigRetail and impacted customers: status, mitigation, ETA to restore dedicated. @sam-sales can you coordinate?

sam-sales: on it. Drafting message now and pulling incident timeline.

ruth-oncall: provisioning update: two spot nodes are stuck, requested on-demand hotfix (4 GPUs) to speed up. Infra says ~9-12m to be usable.

devin-eng: we should also enable KV cache priming on hosted to reduce token usage for repeated prefixes. That will lower served tokens and latency. Turning on now for eu-west hosted pool.

sre-bot: [INFO] kv-cache-priming enabled region=eu-west-1 target_pool=hosted timestamp=2026-03-18T10:15:05Z

ruth-oncall: quick status: dedicated=93% (failed down from 100 after partial drains), hosted fallback=40% active, on-demand 4 GPUs requested, ETA ~11m. No further 502s reported in the last 2m.

leo-infra: next steps: 1) confirm on-demand nodes boot 2) let autoscaler stabilize desired=52 3) revert fallback to normal weights when dedicated <85% 4) postmortem to cover provisioning/backoff logic and earlier alerting thresholds.

devin-eng: adding an alert rule to trigger at dedicated utilization >=85% for 3m so we get earlier heads-up.

ruth-oncall: update: on-demand nodes up and registered at 10:20Z, autoscaler target achieved, dedicated pool back to 86% by 10:26Z. Rolling fallback back to normal (dedicated_weight=0.9).

infra-deploy-bot: action=route-update region=eu-west-1 dedicated_weight=0.9 status=applied ts=2026-03-18T10:26:30Z

ruth-oncall: final: dedicated stable at 72% now, no active 502s, BigRetail notified. Creating postmortem ticket and will follow up on provisioning retry/backoff improvements + cost guardrails. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

anya-product: thanks — please include impact hours and cost delta in the postmortem.

sam-sales: confirmed BigRetail reply: appreciated quick response, will escalate internally but no SLA claim for now.

devin-eng: noted lessons: surface spot vs on-demand failures earlier, add per-region provisioning SLA, and evaluate warm pool of 4 GPUs in eu-west during business hours.

ruth-oncall: closing thread, will create ticket: PM-INC-2026-04 (postmortem: eu-west dedicated provisioning & spillover).
